models.proposals: A consultant-grade deliverable Ravn assembles for a single prospect — six narrative + financial sections plus engagement options, with web-share, PDF, and Slides export.
models.proposalListItem: A compact summary of a proposal used in the project's proposal list rail.
models.recipients: A person on the prospect side who has been granted access to the proposal share link; tracked individually for opens.
models.viewEvents: Each recipient open of the proposal's web view, captured with timestamp, device, and dwell time. Drives the live activity feed and fires owner notifications.
models.engagementOptions: The 2–3 tiered packages a recipient can choose from at acceptance time — name, monthly price, total contract value, scope bullets.
models.financialYears: Year-by-year side-by-side comparison of current SaaS spend vs. Ravn-alternative investment, plus per-year and cumulative savings.

relationships: Each Proposal belongs to one Project and is owned by one Ravn user (ownerEmail).
Each Proposal has many Recipients — recipients live across multiple proposals only via separate records.
Each Proposal has many ViewEvents — each event references the recipient that triggered it (recipientId).
Each Proposal has many EngagementOptions; exactly one option is marked recommended.
Each Proposal carries a 5-year FinancialYears array used to render the comparison chart and savings KPIs.
The proposalListItem array mirrors the proposals collection — UI shows the rail from list items, then opens the matching full Proposal.

proposals.title: Atlas Logistics — Fleet Ops Suite Replacement

cover.tagline: From a $4.2M SaaS sprawl to a single owned platform.

executiveSummary.headline: Replace 11 fragmented SaaS tools with one custom platform Northwind owns.
executiveSummary.subheadline: Net-positive in 14 months, $9.6M cumulative savings over five years.
bullets: Today: $4.2M annual run-rate across 11 tools, with 47% of seats unused and a redundancy rate of 38% across categories.
Tomorrow: a single Ravn-built platform — flight ops, crew comms, ground handling — designed in 18 weeks for the way Northwind actually operates.
Investment: $1.48M one-time build + $260K/yr managed maintenance. Cumulative 5-yr savings of $9.6M against the do-nothing baseline.
Risk: every section below has a paired mitigation. We co-own delivery and exit options stay symmetrical.

currentState.narrative: Northwind's tooling has accreted around shifting org structures. Eleven tools share overlapping ownership across Ops, IT, and Crew Resourcing, and the cost ladder has climbed roughly 18% YoY for three years without a measurable change in adoption. Power-user interviews surfaced specific friction in three categories — fleet scheduling, crew briefing distribution, and ramp-handling intake — that drive the highest seat counts but the lowest weekly active rates.
redundancyCallouts: Crew comms split across Slack Enterprise + AeroBriefr + email (3 tools, 1 outcome).
Fleet scheduling duplicated between FlightStack and a homegrown sheet-based system.
Two CRMs — one for charter sales, one for cargo — that don't share a contact ID.

ravnAlternative.narrative: The Ravn alternative is one purpose-built platform that compresses the 11 tools into a single application Northwind owns. We deliver in three phases — Discovery (3 weeks), Build (12 weeks), and Hardening (3 weeks) — with usable software at the end of every phase, not just the project. AI-assisted development lets us scope features at consultant timeframes that would have been impossible 24 months ago.

riskMitigation.intro: Every custom-build proposal needs a candid risk register. Below are the concerns we've heard from your team mapped to the controls we put in place from day one.

risks.title: Build slips past the 18-week timeline
risks.description: Custom builds historically over-run by 30–40% in enterprise contexts.
risks.mitigation: Fixed-scope phases with shippable software at each gate. We trade scope, never quality, to hold the line.

risks.title: Vendor lock-in inverted (Ravn becomes the new dependency)
risks.description: Replacing 11 vendors with one builder concentrates risk on Ravn.
risks.mitigation: Source code escrow, weekly knowledge-transfer pairings with your engineers, exit clause grants Northwind production access at 30 days notice.

risks.title: Migration disruption to flight ops
risks.description: Flight-day operations cannot tolerate a tooling outage.
risks.mitigation: Dual-run for 6 weeks: legacy tools stay paid until the new platform handles two consecutive 14-day reliability windows.

risks.title: FAA / compliance posture changes
risks.description: Regulatory shifts could force feature changes mid-build.
risks.mitigation: 20% feature buffer in the schedule reserved for compliance-driven scope additions, no-charge.

risks.title: Internal change-management push-back
risks.description: Power users have learned-helplessness around AeroBriefr and FlightStack.
risks.mitigation: Dedicated change-management workstream with 4 onsite training cohorts and a champion network across hubs.
